statement: Venus is the hottest planet in the solar system.
explanation: Venus has an average surface temperature of ~465°C. Its thick CO₂ atmosphere creates a runaway greenhouse effect that traps heat, making it hotter than Mercury despite being further from the Sun.

statement: The Sun is on fire.
explanation: The Sun is not burning in a chemical sense. It generates energy through nuclear fusion — hydrogen atoms fuse to form helium in its core, releasing enormous amounts of energy.

statement: One million Earths could fit inside the Sun.
explanation: The Sun's diameter is about 109 times that of Earth. By volume, approximately 1.3 million Earths could fit inside the Sun.

statement: Saturn is the only planet in our solar system with rings.
explanation: Jupiter, Uranus, and Neptune also have ring systems. Saturn's rings are simply far more prominent and easier to observe from Earth.

statement: Footprints left by Apollo astronauts will remain on the Moon for millions of years.
explanation: The Moon has no atmosphere, wind, or liquid water to erode them. Without these forces, the footprints could remain intact for 10 to 100 million years.

statement: There is no gravity in outer space.
explanation: Gravity extends throughout the universe. The ISS and its crew experience roughly 90% of Earth's surface gravity, but appear weightless because they are in continuous freefall.

statement: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
explanation: Venus rotates on its axis very slowly — one Venusian day lasts 243 Earth days. However, it orbits the Sun in just 225 Earth days, making its day longer than its year.

statement: The Milky Way and the Andromeda galaxy are moving away from each other.
explanation: The Milky Way and Andromeda are on a collision course. They are expected to merge in approximately 4.5 billion years to form a new elliptical galaxy.

statement: Pluto was reclassified from a planet to a dwarf planet in 2006.
explanation: The International Astronomical Union (IAU) redefined 'planet' in 2006, and Pluto did not meet the criteria of 'clearing its orbital neighbourhood', placing it in the dwarf planet category.

statement: Neutron stars are less dense than white dwarf stars.
explanation: A neutron star is one of the densest objects in the universe. A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh approximately 10 million tonnes — far denser than a white dwarf.

statement: The Great Red Spot on Jupiter is a persistent storm system.
explanation: The Great Red Spot is a high-pressure anticyclone wider than Earth. It has been continuously observed since at least the 1830s and may have existed for over 300 years.

statement: All planets in the solar system orbit the Sun in perfect circles.
explanation: As described by Kepler's First Law of Planetary Motion, all planets travel in elliptical orbits with the Sun at one focus, not at the centre of a circle.

statement: Two metal surfaces touching in a vacuum will permanently bond together.
explanation: This is known as cold welding. In space, without an oxide layer to separate them, atoms at the surfaces cannot distinguish between the two pieces of metal and bond spontaneously.

statement: Mars appears red because its surface is covered in rust.
explanation: The Martian surface is rich in iron oxide (Fe₂O₃), the same compound that gives rust its characteristic red-orange colour.

statement: Shooting stars are actual stars falling from the sky.
explanation: Shooting stars are meteors — small fragments of rock or dust that burn up due to friction as they enter Earth's atmosphere at high velocity.

statement: Uranus rotates on its side with an axial tilt of about 98 degrees.
explanation: Uranus has an axial tilt of 97.77°, meaning it essentially rolls around the Sun on its side. This is thought to be the result of a massive collision early in the solar system's history.

statement: The Moon produces its own light.
explanation: The Moon has no light source of its own. It shines by reflecting sunlight off its surface. It reflects approximately 12% of the sunlight that hits it.

statement: Astronauts grow taller in space.
explanation: Without gravity compressing the intervertebral discs, the spine decompresses. Astronauts can grow up to 5 cm (2 inches) taller during a stay on the ISS, reverting after return.

statement: Black holes act like cosmic vacuum cleaners, sucking in everything nearby.
explanation: Black holes exert gravitational attraction like any other mass. Objects at a safe orbital distance remain in orbit around them, just as planets orbit stars.

statement: Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest volcano in the solar system.
explanation: Olympus Mons stands approximately 21.9 km above the Martian datum, nearly three times the height of Mount Everest above sea level.

statement: The Sun appears yellow from Earth because it is yellow.
explanation: The Sun emits white light. It appears yellow or orange from Earth due to Rayleigh scattering, which filters shorter blue wavelengths in the atmosphere.

statement: The Apollo Guidance Computer had less processing power than a modern smartphone.
explanation: The AGC ran at 0.043 MHz with 4 KB of RAM. A modern smartphone processor is millions of times more powerful.

statement: Halley's Comet is visible from Earth approximately every 75–76 years.
explanation: Halley's Comet has an orbital period of about 75.3 years. It was last visible in 1986 and is expected to return in 2061.

statement: Every individual star visible to the naked eye is in our galaxy.
explanation: Every single individual star resolved by the unaided human eye resides within the Milky Way. Distant galaxies like Andromeda appear only as diffuse, hazy smudges rather than individual stars.

statement: Space is completely silent.
explanation: Sound requires a medium to travel through. Interstellar space is an extremely high vacuum, meaning there are not enough molecules to propagate sound waves.

statement: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system.
explanation: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined, and about 11 times wider than Earth.

statement: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.
explanation: It orbits at an average distance of about 58 million kilometres and completes a lap around the Sun every 88 days.

statement: Neptune has the fastest winds of any planet in the solar system.
explanation: Winds on Neptune can exceed 2,000 km/h, far stronger than the strongest storms on Earth.

statement: Mercury rotates exactly three times for every two orbits around the Sun.
explanation: This 3:2 spin-orbit resonance means that a solar day on Mercury lasts two Mercury years.

statement: A light-year is a unit of distance.
explanation: It is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.46 trillion kilometres.

statement: Proxima Centauri is the nearest known star to the Sun.
explanation: It is about 4.24 light-years away, which would take tens of thousands of years to reach with current spacecraft.

statement: The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy.
explanation: Our galaxy has a central bar-shaped structure of stars, with spiral arms extending outward.

statement: The Moon is slowly moving away from Earth.
explanation: It drifts away by about 3.8 centimetres a year, measured using mirrors left on the lunar surface by Apollo astronauts.

statement: Yuri Gagarin was the first human in space.
explanation: He orbited Earth aboard Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961, in a flight that lasted 108 minutes.

statement: Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon.
explanation: He stepped onto the lunar surface on 20 July 1969, followed by Buzz Aldrin.

statement: Valentina Tereshkova was the first woman in space.
explanation: She flew aboard Vostok 6 in June 1963 and orbited Earth 48 times.

statement: Sputnik 1 was the first artificial satellite.
explanation: The Soviet Union launched it in October 1957, starting the space age.

statement: The International Space Station orbits Earth about every 90 minutes.
explanation: It travels at roughly 28,000 km/h, so astronauts see about 16 sunrises and sunsets every day.

statement: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched in 1990.
explanation: Orbiting above the atmosphere, it has produced some of the sharpest views of the universe, including the Hubble Deep Field.

statement: The James Webb Space Telescope observes mainly in infrared light.
explanation: Infrared lets it peer through dust and see very distant galaxies whose light has been stretched by the universe's expansion.

statement: Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object from Earth.
explanation: Launched in 1977, it entered interstellar space in 2012 and is now more than 24 billion kilometres away.

statement: Saturn is less dense than water.
explanation: Its average density is about 0.69 g/cm³, so it would float in a bathtub big enough to hold it.

statement: Saturn's moon Titan has lakes and rivers of liquid methane and ethane.
explanation: Titan is the only moon with a thick atmosphere, and it has weather cycles like Earth's but with hydrocarbons instead of water.

statement: Jupiter's moon Europa is thought to have a salty ocean under its icy crust.
explanation: Scientists think this ocean contains about twice as much water as all of Earth's oceans, making Europa a target in the search for life.

statement: Saturn's moon Enceladus shoots plumes of water vapour into space.
explanation: The Cassini spacecraft flew through the geysers and found salts and organic molecules in the spray.

statement: Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system.
explanation: This moon of Jupiter is bigger than the planet Mercury, although it has less mass.

statement: The Sun contains about 99.8% of the mass of the solar system.
explanation: Everything else, including all the planets, moons and asteroids, makes up just the remaining 0.2%.

statement: The Sun is about 4.6 billion years old.
explanation: It is roughly halfway through its life and will eventually swell into a red giant in about 5 billion years.

statement: A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh billions of tonnes.
explanation: Neutron stars pack more than the mass of the Sun into a ball about 20 km across.

statement: Nothing, not even light, can escape once it passes a black hole's event horizon.
explanation: The event horizon is the boundary where the escape velocity exceeds the speed of light.

statement: The first image of a black hole was released in 2019.
explanation: The Event Horizon Telescope captured the supermassive black hole in the galaxy M87 by linking radio telescopes around the world.

statement: The universe is expanding.
explanation: Observations of distant galaxies moving away from us, first by Edwin Hubble, show that space itself is stretching.

statement: The universe is about 13.8 billion years old.
explanation: This estimate comes from measurements of the cosmic microwave background, the afterglow of the Big Bang.

statement: Mars has two small moons called Phobos and Deimos.
explanation: Both are irregular and potato-shaped, and may be captured asteroids.

statement: Sunsets on Mars appear blue.
explanation: Fine dust in the Martian atmosphere scatters red light away from the Sun, so the sky around the setting Sun looks bluish.

statement: Earth is the densest planet in the solar system.
explanation: Earth's average density is about 5.5 g/cm³, slightly higher than that of any other planet.

statement: Venus rotates in the opposite direction to most planets.
explanation: Venus spins clockwise, backwards compared with Earth, so the Sun rises in the west there.

statement: A comet's tail always points away from the Sun.
explanation: The solar wind and sunlight push material away from the comet, so the tail trails behind on the way in and leads on the way out.

statement: Ceres is a dwarf planet in the asteroid belt.
explanation: It is the largest object in the belt between Mars and Jupiter, and holds a large share of the belt's total mass.

statement: The Moon always shows the same face to Earth.
explanation: It rotates once for every orbit, so one side always faces us, an effect known as tidal locking.

statement: There are more stars in the observable universe than grains of sand on Earth's beaches.
explanation: Astronomers estimate at least 10 sextillion stars, which is far more than the number of sand grains on all of Earth's beaches.

statement: Saturn's rings are made mostly of water ice.
explanation: The rings are billions of pieces of ice and rock, ranging from dust grains to boulders the size of houses.

statement: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun.
explanation: The Moon's shadow falls on Earth, and in the path of totality the day briefly turns dark.

statement: The Sun's core reaches about 15 million degrees Celsius.
explanation: That heat and pressure fuses hydrogen into helium, releasing the energy that powers the Sun.

statement: Sunspots are cooler than the rest of the Sun's surface.
explanation: They are about 1,500 °C cooler and appear dark only by contrast with the brighter surroundings.

statement: NASA's Ingenuity helicopter made the first powered flight on another planet.
explanation: It flew above the surface of Mars on 19 April 2021, and went on to make dozens of flights.

statement: There are 88 officially recognised constellations.
explanation: The International Astronomical Union set the modern list and boundaries in 1922, which cover the entire sky.

statement: Gravitational waves were first detected in 2015.
explanation: The LIGO observatory picked up ripples in spacetime from two merging black holes, a century after Einstein predicted them.

statement: Mercury has water ice at its poles.
explanation: Permanently shadowed craters near Mercury's poles stay cold enough to preserve ice, despite the planet being so close to the Sun.

statement: Mercury is the hottest planet because it is the closest to the Sun.
explanation: Venus is hotter, with surface temperatures around 465 °C, due to its thick atmosphere that traps heat.

statement: The far side of the Moon never receives sunlight.
explanation: The far side gets as much sunlight as the near side; it's just permanently hidden from our view.

statement: The Moon landings were faked.
explanation: The Apollo missions are backed by extensive evidence, including lunar samples, retroreflectors, independent tracking and thousands of photographs.

statement: Jupiter has a solid surface you could stand on.
explanation: Jupiter is a gas giant made mostly of hydrogen and helium, with no solid surface; the deeper you go, the denser the gas becomes.

statement: Mars is the planet that comes closest to Earth.
explanation: Venus gets closer to Earth than Mars ever does, and averaged over time Mercury is the nearest planet to Earth.

statement: The Sun is the largest star in the universe.
explanation: Many stars, such as the red supergiant UY Scuti, are hundreds of times wider than the Sun.

statement: The Big Bang was an explosion that happened at one point in space.
explanation: The Big Bang was an expansion of space itself everywhere at once, not an explosion into existing space.

statement: Space is so cold that anything exposed to it freezes instantly.
explanation: A vacuum is a poor conductor of heat, so an object loses heat slowly, mostly by radiation.

statement: An astronaut's body would explode if exposed to the vacuum of space.
explanation: Skin is strong enough to hold the body together; the real dangers are lack of oxygen and loss of consciousness within seconds.

statement: The Moon has no gravity.
explanation: The Moon has about one-sixth of Earth's gravity, which is why astronauts could bounce along its surface.

statement: Saturn's rings are solid, continuous sheets.
explanation: They are made of countless separate particles orbiting Saturn, from tiny grains to large boulders.

statement: The asteroid belt is so crowded that spacecraft must dodge rocks.
explanation: The asteroids are spread across millions of kilometres, and spacecraft have crossed the belt without ever coming close to one.

statement: Earth is the only place in the solar system with liquid water.
explanation: Evidence suggests liquid water oceans lie beneath the ice of moons such as Europa and Enceladus.

statement: Mars's atmosphere is mostly oxygen.
explanation: It is about 95% carbon dioxide, and extremely thin, so humans can't breathe it.

statement: A light-year is a measure of time.
explanation: A light-year is a measure of distance: how far light travels in one year.

statement: The stars in a constellation are all close together in space.
explanation: They only appear to be near each other from Earth, and may be at wildly different distances.

statement: The Moon is physically larger when it is near the horizon.
explanation: This is an optical illusion; the Moon's real size and apparent size in the sky stay the same.

statement: Humans have already travelled to Mars.
explanation: Only robotic spacecraft such as rovers and landers have reached Mars so far.

statement: Rocket engines need air to push against in order to work in space.
explanation: Rockets work by expelling exhaust, which pushes the rocket forward according to Newton's third law, and they work best in a vacuum.

statement: Stars twinkle because their brightness pulses on and off.
explanation: Twinkling is caused by Earth's turbulent atmosphere bending starlight, and stars seen from space do not twinkle.

statement: The phases of the Moon are caused by Earth's shadow.
explanation: Phases occur because we see different amounts of the Moon's sunlit half as it orbits; Earth's shadow causes lunar eclipses.

statement: It is safe to look at a partial solar eclipse without eye protection.
explanation: Even a partially covered Sun can burn the retina and damage your eyes permanently.

statement: The Milky Way is the only galaxy in the universe.
explanation: The observable universe contains hundreds of billions of galaxies.

statement: Meteorites are red-hot when they land on Earth.
explanation: A meteorite's surface melts in the atmosphere, but the interior stays cold after travelling through space, so they are often cool to the touch.

statement: The Sun will end its life as a supernova.
explanation: The Sun is not massive enough; it will swell into a red giant and then shed its outer layers to become a white dwarf.

statement: Earth sits at the centre of the Milky Way.
explanation: The Solar System is about 26,000 light-years from the galactic centre, in one of the spiral arms.

statement: Polaris, the North Star, is the brightest star in the night sky.
explanation: Polaris is only about the 48th-brightest star; its fame comes from sitting almost directly above the North Pole.

statement: Venus is the planet closest to the Sun.
explanation: Mercury is closest to the Sun; Venus is second.

statement: The Sun is the hottest kind of star there is.
explanation: The Sun's surface is about 5,500 °C, while blue stars can have surfaces over 30,000 °C.

statement: Venus is a star, because it shines brightly in the night sky.
explanation: Venus is a planet and shines by reflecting sunlight, and its thick, cloudy atmosphere makes it very reflective.

statement: Mars has no water at all.
explanation: Mars has water ice at its poles and underground, and there is evidence that liquid water once flowed across its surface.
